text:
alex (support): FYI: CS reporting spike of 503s starting ~23:38 UTC from multiple customers (acme, helix). error shows upstream worker crash. @ravi can you triage?

ravi (eng-oncall): on it. pulling logs now, adding @maria for SRE context. which pool?

alex (support): affect appears limited to us-west-2 gpu-pool-sterling. customers saw timeouts first then 503s. req ids: r=acme/0x9f7a, r=helix/0x7b2c

deploy-bot: Deployment "hosted-infer/runtime-v2.14.1" started at 2026-03-17T23:35:12Z to pool gpu-pool-sterling

sam (eng-runtime): seeing repeated crashes in infer-runner on infer-3: SIGSEGV in attention_kern.cu, then container restart. example from /var/log/infer-runner.log:

```
Mar 17 23:38:42 infer-runner[2147]: ERROR: worker 3 crashed: signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
Mar 17 23:38:42 infer-runner[2147]: backtrace: libruntime.so(+0x12f4a) [0x7f1c2f4f]
Mar 17 23:38:42 infer-runner[2147]: cudaErrorIllegalAddress at attention_kern.cu:312
Mar 17 23:38:42 infer-runner[2147]: last_kv_prefetch_size=1248576000 bytes, batch_count=48
Mar 17 23:38:42 infer-runner[2147]: OOM? nvmlEvent: GPU 0 memory spike -> cgroup kill
```

maria (sre): are these crashes correlated with the deploy? deploy-bot shows 23:35 UTC which is just before spikes
ravi (eng-oncall): possibly correlated. timeline: deploy -> sudden auth-batched embed traffic from acme/helix -> worker crashes. hypothesis: new kernel + large prefetch combined with massive batchmap causing mem oversubscription

kevin (customer-success): customers reported rising latency for ~2m before failures and then partial billing errors (some requests charged but errored). CS needs an update to send to acme.

alex (support): drafting a short customer note now, will include mitigation steps and ETA once we have them :writing_hand:

sam (eng-runtime): immediate repro I ran: send 40 concurrent embed jobs with batch_size=128, context tokens ~65k each. curl sample:

```
for i in {1..40}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"embed-xl","inputs":["<very-large-payload>"],"batch_size":128}' &
done
```

On infer-3 this reproduced segfaults within ~30s.

maria (sre): mitigation idea: throttle concurrent burst, reduce max batch_size at gateway, and restart the crashed worker group so they come up with reduced prefetch settings. can we apply a gateway rate-limit for pool=sterling?
ravi (eng-oncall): yes. action plan: 1) push temporary gateway throttles for pool=sterling (limit concurrent embed jobs to 12) 2) restart runner group on infer-3/4 with env INFER_KV_PREFETCH=off 3) revert new runtime if crashes persist. rolling restart to avoid global outage.

alex (support): noted. CS will tell customers we're applying throttles and restarts; ETA 10m for initial mitigation.

ravi (eng-oncall): applying throttle now -> runbook command:

```
# set concurrent embed limit for pool
rctl set gateway --pool gpu-pool-sterling --route "/v1/embeddings" --concurrency 12 --duration 1h --reason "mitigate segfault bursts"
```

maria (sre): restarting runner group (infer-3, infer-4) with reduced prefetch flag

```
ssh infra@infra-proxy
kubectl -n hosted-infer set env ds/infer-runner INFER_KV_PREFETCH=false --selector=pool=sterling
kubectl -n hosted-infer rollout restart ds/infer-runner -l pool=sterling
```

ravi (eng-oncall): restart kicked off. monitoring logs and metrics.

~2m later
ravi (eng-oncall): initial metrics: error rate in pool dropped from 7.9% -> 0.8% after throttle + restart. latency p95 improved. still seeing a small tail of restarts on a single host (infer-5)
sam (eng-runtime): infer-5 logs show repeated KV cache reclaim thrash, suggest lowering prefetch window in runtime config permanently and adding a safety cap on per-request token counts.

kevin (customer-success): CS update sent to acme/helix: "We've applied throttles and are restarting affected workers; you may see degraded throughput for ~10-20 minutes. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." :email:

alex (support): CS asked about billing: will customers be credited for partial failures? finance wants list of impacted req ids.
maria (sre): we can export req ids from kube logs and billing traces. I'll run an extraction job and post CSV to the incident ticket.

ravi (eng-oncall): current short-term mitigation holding. next steps: deeper RCA to confirm interaction between runtime kernel change in v2.14.1 and large prefetch batchmap; follow-ups: add gateway-level per-request token cap (e.g. 100k tokens), add runtime guard to disable aggressive kv prefetch when concurrent batch_count > 24, and staged rollback if we see regression in next 24h.

sam (eng-runtime): filing a PR with conservative prefetch default + telemetry to detect memory oversubscription. PR: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/542

maria (sre): tagging for postmortem and scheduling blameless RCA meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

alex (support): closing the customer-facing loop for now. will reopen thread if errors reappear. :thumbsup:
